It calls only relative `/ui/*` URLs. nginx serves the built app on port 80 (published as 4200) and proxies `/ui/*` to `${BFF_URL}` with buffering off and a 300 s read timeout; in development `ng serve` with `proxy.conf.json` does the same.

about.base: Takes what the Analysis engine returns and shapes it into exactly what one screen needs. Holds no lottery logic of its own.

OpenAPI at `/v3/api-docs`, from which the website generates its types.

about.base:
The suite in one line: the user uses the **website**, the website asks the **Screen API**, the Screen API asks the **Analysis engine**, and the engine gets its draw history from the **Results store**, which keeps itself current from the **Texas Lottery website**.

Click any part for what it does; the other views go one level deeper.

The same suite one level down: what each part contains and which parts talk to each other.

Requests flow from the top down. Draw data flows the other way: the **Results updater** downloads it and the **Draw history service** hands it to the engine.
The Maven modules of **lotto-options-core** by dependency. The Screen API shares only the data formats with the engine.

title.base: A tour of the Lotto suite

about.base: The user opens the **website** in a browser and picks a state and a game.
The **Screen API** prepares the data for each screen. It has no lottery logic of its own.
The **Analysis engine** does the thinking: dashboards, generated picks, scoring and betslips.

set.exec: The **engine** is where the value is: it turns past draws into suggested picks.

add.engineer: One Spring Boot jar on port 8002, built from the modules in the Engineering view.

about.base: Inside the engine, **Pick generation** runs the strategy the user chose and scores the tickets against past draws.
The **Results store** keeps every past draw and refreshes them from the Texas Lottery website every two hours.
Inside the store, the updater downloads new results, the reader turns them into draws, and the history service answers the engine.
Now follow one request: what happens when the user clicks **Generate**.
The whole suite again.
